title: Hearing Charlie Christian over the BBC
summary: Drunk on champagne and rum in Europe, Butler was sobered by Christian's guitar on the BBC and felt he affected him like Oscar Ellman.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: You'll hear about him no matter where you at, you'll hear him somewhere, because Charlie Christian, in fact, I'd been drinking champagne and rum which is most dangerous to drink.
And my head was torn up and I turned my radio on, and I got the BBC and I heard so much guitar that it sobered me up.

And that was the BBC and the guitarist -- Charlie Christian. You see, you hear these things no matter where you get to hear them. There's radios in every country. That's the first time I heard him. That was it. I knew. Because I, you see, it gives you the same effect, understand? Like there are certain people who give you the same effect as another person. For example, you may be talking to someone and you say, well, this man effects me the same way that Jacques effects me.
